args.rationale: Applying the firm's hearsay rule memo (FRE 801) to Scenario A: For the north silo exhaust fan defect claim, we intend to offer the out-of-court oral statement by foreman Della Kite to warehouse worker Tobias Prell — "the north silo fan has been shorting for weeks" — made in the loading yard, not in a court proceeding. Under the memo Section 1, hearsay requires both elements: (a) the statement was made outside the current trial, and (b) it is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted. Here, the client letter states the purpose is "to prove that the fan really had been shorting — that is, to prove the truth of what Ms. Kite said." Per memo Section 4, this stated purpose is controlling. Ms. Kite's remark is an out-of-court oral assertion offered to prove the fan was in fact defective/shorting — i.e., for the truth of the matter asserted. Both hearsay elements are satisfied, so the item IS hearsay under the memo's test. Determination: approved (hearsay).
